grades.lower_bound_mechanism: Multiples of theta are universally winning (split k*theta = theta + (k-1)*theta, both children carry a multiple); for a generic triangle cut the max angle at r = ceil(p/theta)*theta - p so C1 gets 180-(p+r) and C2 gets p+r, both multiples; theta=90 handled separately by x=90-p
grades.upper_bound_mechanism: Invariant I: no angle is an integer multiple of theta; four-case analysis shows some child stays in I, the last case needing 180 not a multiple of theta
grades.notes: Complete on all four obligations: correct answer, additive lemma with both children covered, winning strategy for every initial triangle and every discard (including n=2), and a fully verified invariant for the avoidance direction. Minor terseness in nonemptiness of I and in the n=2 angle conditions, but arguments are checkable.
